world.h: Yemen's government opens major Houthi offensive
world.b: Yemen's government announced a major offensive against the Houthis.
more: Iran said there is no military solution to its conflict with the United States and that it is ready to defend itself if the US attacks.

world.h: Ethiopian forces retake Tigray capital Mekelle
world.b: Federal forces and allied fighters captured Mekelle on Saturday after the Tigray People's Liberation Front withdrew from the city.
more: The fighting comes less than four years after the 2022 Pretoria agreement ended a war that killed hundreds of thousands.
Explosions were reported in Addis Ababa, and Ethiopia cut diplomatic ties with Eritrea, which it accuses of backing opposition forces.

world.h: US pulls B-1 bombers from UK's RAF Fairford
world.b: The US Air Force removed its bombers from the British air base after several terrorism-related arrests were made outside it.
more: Al Jazeera reported the bombers were redeployed to the United States amid fears linked to Iran.

world.h: Four leaders call for peace as Ethiopia war grows
world.b: The leaders of Egypt, Eritrea, Somalia and Sudan's army met in New Alamein City, Egypt, and called for political and peaceful solutions to regional conflicts.
more: Their declaration backed Sudan's military government.
It opposed what it called unilateral measures by Ethiopia over the Nile dam and access to the Red Sea.

national.h: Search ends for six aboard crashed medical jet
national.b: The Coast Guard suspended its search for six people aboard a medical jet that crashed on a flight from Bermuda to Boston.
more: Crews searched 4,445 miles over about 66 hours and confirmed debris found off Nantucket came from the plane.
Aboard were two Canadian pilots, two Canadian medical workers, a Bermudian patient and a family escort.
The cause of the crash has not been determined.

national.h: 'Jane Doe' posts back Cornell rape lawsuit
national.b: Many women, and some men, posted that they were Jane Doe, in support of a woman suing Cornell University and seven fraternity members she accuses of raping her.

politics.h: Trump picks Jay Clayton to lead new AI task force
politics.b: President Trump named Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton to lead a new federal AI task force he calls the Super Intelligence Force.
more: Members include FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson, Pentagon technology chief Emil Michael and personnel director Scott Kupor.
It follows a White House meeting where AI executives signed a voluntary accord to police their own technology.

politics.h: KKK tries to rebrand as the 'Knights Party'
politics.b: The hate group is trying to rebrand itself as the Knights Party in an attempt to grow its base, Al Jazeera reports.

politics.h: Despair fuels political anxiety among students
politics.b: College students' worry about the future is fueling restlessness with a national political system they fear can no longer improve, PBS reports.

international.h: Brazil heads to Lula-Bolsonaro run-off Oct 25
international.b: Flavio Bolsonaro won 47% of valid votes to President Lula's 44.9%, so neither won outright.
more: Bolsonaro got about 56 million votes to Lula's nearly 53 million.
Bolsonaro's Liberal Party is set to become the largest party in the Chamber of Deputies.

international.h: Malaysia sends 1,479 people back to Myanmar
international.b: Nearly 1,500 Myanmar nationals arrived in Yangon on Sunday aboard navy and hospital ships from Malaysia, despite UN warnings.
more: Malaysia plans to send back 5,000 people in stages and holds more than 10,300 others in immigration detention.
The UN refugee agency said its staff were not allowed to meet the returnees to confirm they chose freely to go back.
Rights groups warn returnees face persecution and forced conscription in Myanmar's civil war.

international.h: Singapore turns matchmaker as births hit low
international.b: Singapore is turning matchmaker as its birthrate sits at rock-bottom levels, Al Jazeera reports.

international.h: Nicaragua to quit Central American Parliament
international.b: Nicaragua says it will withdraw from the Central American Parliament.

international.h: France to close up to 500 schools amid protests
international.b: Up to 500 schools across France will be totally or partly closed on Monday because of protests by teenage pupils, the education minister said.
more: Protests disrupted more than 730 schools last week, The Local reported.

business.h: OPEC+ keeps oil output steady for November
business.b: Seven major oil exporters, including Saudi Arabia and Russia, agreed to keep production steady in November as Brent crude stayed above $100 a barrel.
more: The group will meet again on November 1.
The Group of Seven plans to release 100 million barrels of oil and fuel, including a large diesel release within 20 days.

science.h: Nobel medicine prize goes to optogenetics pioneers
science.b: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel won the 2026 Nobel Prize in physiology or medicine for work on light-gated ion channels and optogenetics.
more: Their work created a light-controlled switch to turn nerve cells in the brain on and off.
Hegemann and Nagel found a protein in green algae that opens an electrical channel in blue light.
Deisseroth used its gene to make nerve cells in living mouse brains respond to light.

sports.h: Lamb's 17 catches lift Cowboys past Texans 34-30
sports.b: CeeDee Lamb caught 17 passes for 189 yards, including the 12-yard game-winning touchdown with 40 seconds left.
more: It set a Cowboys record for catches by a wide receiver in a game.

sports.h: Dream beat Liberty 92-82 in semifinal opener
sports.b: Jordin Canada scored 25 points with five steals as Atlanta took Game 1 of the WNBA semifinals.
more: The Dream forced 21 Liberty turnovers and turned them into 32 points.

sports.h: Packers fear Cooper tore his Achilles
sports.b: Green Bay fears linebacker Edgerrin Cooper suffered a season-ending torn Achilles in Sunday's win over Tampa Bay.

sports.h: Alabama jumps Indiana in AP Top 25
sports.b: Alabama moved ahead of Indiana in the AP college football rankings ahead of its game with Georgia.

goodnews.h: Man catches child who fell from balcony in Egypt
goodnews.b: Video shows a man in Egypt rushing to catch a young boy who fell from a second-floor balcony.
more: The child hit a washing line on the way down, giving the man crucial extra time to reach him.

goodnews.h: Dakar neighbours clean up school for new year
goodnews.b: Students, teachers and volunteers in Dakar, Senegal, cleaned Medina Gounass Elementary School on Saturday ahead of the new academic year.
more: They swept classrooms, cleared drains and removed plastic and household waste.
Organizers said the effort also aimed to raise awareness about protecting the environment.

local.h: Mamdani to clear 10,000 families off childcare waitlist
local.b: The city will move 10,000 low-income families off the waitlist for subsidized childcare, Mayor Mamdani announced.
more: More than 16,000 families are waiting for the Child Care Assistance Program, which serves families earning up to $116,000 a year for a family of four.
Governor Kathy Hochul is putting $475 million toward the backlog that built up since May 2025.

local.h: Two killed in Queens and Brooklyn crashes
local.b: A hit-and-run on Monday killed a 62-year-old man, and a crash involving an impaired driver on Sunday killed a 23-year-old woman, police said.

local.h: NY's stockpiled abortion pills have all expired
local.b: In 2023 the state bought 150,000 misoprostol pills, enough for 12,500 doses, for $112,000. Now they are all expired.

local.h: Legionnaires' outbreaks spark NYC water debate
local.b: A group backed by cooling tower companies wants the city to filter all drinking water; experts dispute that it is needed.

local.h: City Council hearing to spotlight AI risks
local.b: Tech workers and whistleblowers will testify to the City Council about the dangers of artificial intelligence.

local.h: Sixth person dies after falling ill in NYPD custody
local.b: The 54-year-old was hospitalized twice after his arrest Friday, police said.

periods.name: Monday
periods.text: Sunny, with a high near 69. Breezy, with a northwest wind 9 to 14 mph increasing to 16 to 21 mph in the afternoon.

periods.name: Monday Night
periods.text: Clear, with a low around 50. Northwest wind 13 to 15 mph.

periods.name: Tuesday
periods.text: Sunny, with a high near 63. Northwest wind 9 to 11 mph.

periods.name: Tuesday Night
periods.text: Clear, with a low around 50. West wind 3 to 7 mph.

periods.name: Wednesday Night
periods.text: Mostly clear, with a low around 56.

localgood.h: Banned books and Pooh at NYC libraries
localgood.b: NYC libraries mark Banned Books Week this October, with Queens Public Library offering free banned titles.
more: NYPL is celebrating Winnie the Pooh's centennial with movies, readings and crafts across the boroughs.
